h: The Shepherd of Yisrael and Eating That Gives Life

p: At the third meal we say the psalm
that David HaMelech, peace be upon him, said:
ה׳ רוֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר (תְּהִלִּים כג, א)
"Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack" (Tehillim 23:1);
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר
and likewise Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, said
from my beginning until this day."
And it is stated in the Gemara (Taanis 5b):
וְכֵן בְּדָוִד מָצִינוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כה, א)
And so too regarding David we find (Rosh Hashanah 25a):
David, King of Yisrael, lives and endures";
"David came to life at that moment."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת ל, א)
This is along the lines of what they said (Shabbos 30a):
"In your lifetime I will not make it known;
בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ וְכוּלֵּי
in the lifetime of Shlomo your son I will make it known, etc."
And it is as we said,
when the eating is in holiness,
for then he automatically merits eternal life.
וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן הוּא גַּם כֵּן עֵצָה לָזֶה
Birkas HaMazon is likewise a means for this,
so that the eating not bring one
to the accusation of the yetzer hara,
"And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless";
that is, by knowing and recognizing
that Hashem Yisbarach is the One Who feeds and sustains;
and eating that comes from Hashem Yisbarach
לֹא יָבִיא לִידֵי קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע
will not lead to the accusation of the yetzer hara.
And the Sages instituted a berachah before it as well,
and the washing of the hands.
"'And you shall sanctify yourselves': this is the first water, etc."
so that the eating can be in holiness.
Therefore Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
for his eating was in holiness,
and he knew nothing at all of bodily pleasure,
שֶׁהָיָה כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל
being like Adam HaRishon before the corruption,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
and "the embalmers embalmed him and the eulogizers eulogized him,"
"Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust."
"'When you walk, it shall lead you' (Mishlei 6:22):
'when you lie down, it shall watch over you':
'and when you awake, it shall speak with you':
That is, when in This World
and you know that Hashem is my shepherd,
it will be like sleep and awakening;
"And many of those who sleep in the dust."
who said, "And I did not benefit
from whose table there never ceased
only his eating was in holiness,
וְלֹא הִרְגִּישׁ שׁוּם הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף כְּלָל
and did not feel any bodily pleasure at all.
(in Megaleh Amukos by Rabbeinu Nosson Shapira, Vayeitzei):
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (כְּתוּבּוֹת קג, א)
That is why it is stated in the Gemara (Kesubos 103a):
he would come to his house, etc.,"
And likewise David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who became a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
"That of the Table, David merited it and took it";
only that in his lifetime he did not trust himself
and would fast, as we said;
"at that moment David came to life,"
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר ה׳ רוֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר
And this is what he said: "Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack,"
for then, since his eating is in holiness,
וְזֶה גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת
And this is "Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death,
לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי
I will fear no evil, for You are with me"
"When you walk, it shall lead you;
when you lie down, it shall watch over you;
and when you awake, it shall speak with you,"

p: וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג קפח, ב)
And in the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 188b):
"'And it shall be, when you eat, etc.' (Bamidbar 15:19):
תְּנוּ כָבוֹד לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם (יִרְמְיָה יג, טז)
to the Holy One, blessed is He, etc."
for the purpose of creation was
that they recognize the power of His kingship, may His Name be blessed;
כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
"Everything that the Holy One, blessed is He, created in His world,
He created only for His honor, etc."
And this is "honor to Hashem your God."
לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
"The Holy One, blessed is He, created His world
only so that they should fear Him,
That is, the attribute of Malchus,
to which the Name Adnus corresponds,
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?"
who is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus and fear,
and he shall read in it all the days of his life,
so that he may learn to fear, etc.";
have the Torah standing before his eyes.
And it is stated in the Gemara (Berachos 34b):
because he is the root of fear;
and that is why he merited the table of kings,
that the eating be in holiness,
And Malchus is the aspect of speech,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א לב, א)
as is written in the holy Zohar (I 32a):
and Shabbos is the aspect of Malchus;
for the whole essence of the conduct of kingship
that he issues a decree and it is fulfilled.
And this is "give a mouth, give honor";
and this is what the waved Omer signifies
at the beginning of the harvest:
that they recognize that Hashem Yisbarach
is the One Who feeds and nourishes,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָאֲכִילָה הוּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
and through this the eating is in holiness,
and this is "Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack."
כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה לַאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
every one of Yisrael merits eating in holiness,
and the eating is from the side of the Tree of Life,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן זוֹכִין לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
and thereby we merit eternal life.
In the Midrashim and the Yerushalmi
they refer to death as "when he slept,"
meaning that it is only like sleep;
but there this is said of great people.
"an incident with a certain band of wanton men, etc.,
who used to eat and drink in the synagogue
And although it calls them wanton,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא שָׁם עַל הַמִּיתָה
nevertheless it uses for the death
which is a term of sleep.
But because it is mentioned of them
that they ate every Friday night,
and one who keeps Shabbos merits eternal life,
as they said, "those who taste it merit life."
as is brought (in the Gemara, Shabbos 118b, in the Midrashim,
and in the holy Zohar in several places);
and then all the blemish would be rectified,
as in the Time to Come.
But the world is judged by its majority;
and although death has not yet been abolished,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא רַק כְּשֵׁינָה וִיקִיצָה
nevertheless it is only like sleep and awakening.
And this is why it says there,
because they were keepers of Shabbos.
And especially at the third meal,
which is "the river that goes out of Eden
which is the entire middle line,
that the eating be in holiness.
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג קצג, א)
And in the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 193a):
That he would set a table
it should have said 'by the rivers,'
since it is called Aram Naharayim;
for it always stands by one river."
That is, just as in holiness
to draw down the holy spirit from above to below,
as is written in the holy Zohar earlier
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַנָּהָר הַיּוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן
and this is through the river that goes out of Eden
יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן נָהָר קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי
there is likewise a river, the middle line,
that he would set for the Other Side,
as is written in the holy Zohar.
Therefore at this meal we say,
in the middle of the meal,
"Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack."
וְאַחַר שֶׁעָבַר כָּל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת בִּשְׁמִירָה
And after the entire day of Shabbos has passed in keeping it,
is redeemed from all the blemishes
as they said, "those who taste it merit life,"
we say, "Even when I walk, etc.,
לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי
I will fear no evil, for You are with me,"
for we merit eternal life, as stated.
